entries.notes: 0329 shipped the owner check and the very next read returned four rows reading ready, which was consistent with two different worlds: the new code running and those four being Darrell's own, or the old code still on the box and the owner check not yet in play. The census reaches the NAS by the services-sync pull, so its version is always a question, and the receipt published the builder's code sha and never its own. entries.task: The census can actually name its own code, because HEAD is read from files rather than through git
entries.notes: DR-1517 shipped census_code_sha as git rev-parse and the field never arrived: 59 minutes and about four services-sync cycles after merge, two separate reads still printed that the census did not name its own code. Not a pull delay - DR-1511's census change had appeared 16 minutes after its merge, one cycle, so code refresh works and this one call was failing. Every likely cause is a property of the subprocess rather than the question: git off the PATH of whichever user the clock runs the census as, or git refusing a mirror it does not own with fatal detected dubious ownership, which the shape test correctly turned into unknown instead of publishing a sentence. The files answer the same question with no PATH, no ownership check and no subprocess: .git/HEAD, the ref file, and packed-refs. A test harness that raises if git is called proves the files come first rather than merely being preferred. The cause on the NAS is explicitly NOT confirmed - the sandbox cannot reach the box - so what is claimed is only that the subprocess form never answered while a file read cannot fail for any of those reasons.
